examples.en: A newborn baby wakes up often all day long.
A newborn baby was born next door.

examples.ko: 갓난아기를 안을 때는 목을 받쳐 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When you hold a newborn baby, you need to support the neck.
I could hear a newborn baby crying all night.

examples.ko: 갓난아기 때 제 사진을 보니 신기해요.
examples.en: It's amazing to see a picture of me as a newborn.
My nephew is a newborn, so I came to buy a gift.

explain: 막 태어난 아기를 말해요. '갓난아이', '갓난애'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 병원에서 쓰는 '신생아'는 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.

phrases.en: The newborn is sleeping in its mother's arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갓난아기'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 갓난아기.

phrases.en: The newborn next door cries all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갓난아이'를 줄인 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, shortened form of 갓난아이.

phrases.en: I held the newborn baby carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 품에 안을 때 '안다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 안다 is used for holding a baby in your arms.

explain_en: It refers to a baby who has just been born. '갓난아이' and '갓난애' are used with the same meaning. '신생아', used in hospitals, sounds a bit more formal.

en: to become independent; to move out on one's own

examples.en: I will move out of my parents' house next year.
My older brother became independent at twenty.
If you move out on your own, living alone costs money.
I left the company and opened a small shop.
An independent country makes its own laws.
When do you plan to become independent?

explain: 한국에서는 대학을 졸업하거나 취직한 뒤 부모님 집에서 나가 혼자 사는 것을 '독립하다'라고 많이 말해요. 나라가 다른 나라에서 벗어날 때도 쓰고, 직장에서 나와 자기 일을 시작할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I graduated from university and now live on my own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '독립하다'에 '-아서/어서 살다'를 붙여, 부모님 집을 나와 혼자 사는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 'to live' to say you moved out and now live independently.

phrases.en: I want to move out on my own soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-고 싶다' to express a wish to become independent.

phrases.example: 스무 살이 되면 경제적으로 독립할 거예요.
phrases.en: When I turn twenty, I will become financially independent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 나가는 것만이 아니라 돈 문제에서 혼자 서는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means standing on your own financially, not only moving out.

explain_en: In Korea, moving out of your parents' home to live alone, usually after graduating or getting a job, is commonly called '독립하다'. It also describes a country breaking away from another, and leaving a job to start your own work.

dis.h: become independent by own action; move out

p.n: The passive verb does not fit a person moving out on their own.

en: arranged meeting for marriage; blind date with a potential spouse

examples.ko: 이모가 소개해 준 사람과 맞선을 봤어요.
examples.en: I went on a matchmaking meeting with someone my aunt introduced.
At the matchmaking meeting, we talked about our hobbies.
It is my first matchmaking meeting, so I am very nervous.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 맞선이 있어서 옷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I have a matchmaking meeting this evening, so I bought clothes.
The two who met through a matchmaking meeting got married.

examples.ko: 이번 주말 맞선에 입고 갈 옷을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose what to wear to this weekend's matchmaking meeting.

explain: '맞선을 보다'라고 말해요. 결혼을 생각하고 소개받은 사람을 만나는 자리라서, 가벼운 만남인 '소개팅'과는 분위기가 달라요.

phrases.en: I'm going on an arranged meeting this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞선'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 말로, 결혼을 생각하고 소개받은 사람을 만난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 맞선; it means meeting someone introduced to you with marriage in mind.
phrases.en_equiv: to go on an arranged meeting

phrases.en: I was very nervous at the arranged meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞선을 하는 자리나 그 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the occasion or setting of the meeting itself.

phrases.en: I liked the person I met at the arranged meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞선에서 만난 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person you meet at the meeting.

explain_en: The usual phrase is 맞선을 보다 (literally 'see' a matchmaking meeting). Since it is a meeting with an introduced person with marriage in mind, its mood differs from a casual blind date.

examples.ko: 사진가는 하루 종일 산에서 해를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The photographer waited for the sun on the mountain all day.
A famous photographer came to our school.
I am a student who dreams of becoming a photographer.
I asked a photographer to take our family photo.

examples.ko: 그 사진가의 전시회가 다음 주에 열려요.
examples.en: That photographer's exhibition opens next week.
My father's friend works as a travel photographer.

explain: 사진을 찍는 일을 직업으로 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 같은 일을 하는 사람을 '사진작가'라고도 하고, 사진관에서 일하는 사람은 '사진사'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The photographer is taking pictures of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사진가'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 작품을 만드는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 사진가 but with more of an artist feel.

phrases.en: I want to become a photographer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 '이/가 되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual way to talk about a dream job.

phrases.en: Landscape photographers get up at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 찍는 대상을 붙여 어떤 사진가인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the subject before it to say what kind of photographer.

explain_en: It refers to a person who takes photos as a profession. The same person may also be called '사진작가', and someone working at a photo studio is sometimes called '사진사'.

examples.ko: 어머니는 스무 살에 이 마을로 시집오셨어요.
examples.en: My mother came to this village as a bride at twenty.

examples.ko: 외국에서 시집온 며느리가 한국말을 아주 잘해요.
examples.en: The daughter-in-law who married in from abroad speaks Korean very well.
It's my first holiday since marrying into the family, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 제가 시집왔을 때는 이 동네가 지금과 많이 달랐어요.
examples.en: When I first came here as a bride, this neighborhood was very different from now.
They say my grandmother came as a bride from a distant village.

examples.ko: 시집오기 전에는 요리를 거의 못 했어요.
examples.en: Before I got married and came here, I could hardly cook.

explain: 여자가 결혼해서 남편 집안의 일원이 되는 것을 시댁 쪽에서 볼 때 써요. 반대로 친정 쪽에서 보면 '시집가다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I have lived ten years since I came to Korea to marry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼해서 온 뒤의 생활을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue talking about life after marrying in.

phrases.en: Before I married and came here, I lived in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼하기 전의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about things before marriage.

phrases.en: My aunt got married early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친정 쪽에서 보면 '시집가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: From the bride's own family's side, use 시집가다.

explain_en: It is used when a woman marries and joins her husband's family, seen from the husband's family side. From her own family's side, you use '시집가다' instead.

en: to date; to be in a romantic relationship

examples.en: I dated in college.
The two dated for three years and got married.
These days I'm busy and have no time to date.
My friend is in a relationship and looks happy.

examples.ko: 연애하면 좋은 점도 있고 힘든 점도 있어요.
examples.en: Dating has good points and hard points.
I heard a couple who dated for a long time broke up.

explain: '연애하다'는 서로 좋아하는 사이로 만나는 것을 말해요. '사귀다'는 '누구와 사귀어요'처럼 상대를 말할 때 편하고, '연애하다'는 연애하는 일 자체를 말할 때 자주 써요. '연애를 하다'처럼 '연애'와 '하다'를 나눠 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 작년부터 그 사람과 사귀고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been going out with that person since last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '누구와 사귀다'처럼 상대를 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy when you name the other person, as in 'go out with someone'.

phrases.en: The two of them are dating these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 연애하는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe being in a relationship now.

phrases.en: The two of them dated for a long time and then got married.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연애한 기간이 길다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the relationship lasted a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: to date for a long time

explain_en: 연애하다 means being in a romantic relationship. 사귀다 is handy when you name the partner, as in '누구와 사귀어요', while 연애하다 talks about the activity of dating itself. You can also split it as '연애를 하다'.

p.n: The replacement is more casual and focuses on going on dates.

examples.en: I was a boarder during university.

examples.ko: 하숙집 아주머니는 하숙생들에게 밥을 해 주세요.
examples.en: The landlady cooks meals for the boarders.
I heard one more boarder is moving in.
I became friends with the boarder in the next room.
A boarder has to pay for the room every month.

examples.ko: 우리 집에도 하숙생을 받아 볼까 해요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of taking in a boarder at our house too.

explain: 하숙은 남의 집에서 방을 빌리고 보통 식사도 함께 받는 거예요. 혼자 방을 구해서 직접 해 먹으며 사는 '자취생'과 구별해서 말해요.

phrases.en: I live in a boarding house near the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하숙생이 사는 집이에요. 사람은 '하숙생', 집은 '하숙집'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The house where a lodger lives. The person is 하숙생, the house is 하숙집.

phrases.en: I board in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하숙생으로 사는 일을 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for living as a boarder.

phrases.en: I eat dinner with my fellow boarders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 하숙집에서 사는 친구를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For friends who live in the same boarding house.

explain_en: '하숙' means renting a room in someone's house, usually with meals included. It is different from a '자취생', who rents a place alone and cooks for themselves.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 달부터 요리 학원에서 훈련생으로 일해요.
examples.en: From this month I work as a trainee at a cooking academy.

examples.ko: 훈련생들은 아침 일곱 시부터 운동장에 모여요.
examples.en: The trainees gather on the field from seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 훈련생이 열 명 정도 새로 들어왔어요.
examples.en: About ten new trainees have joined.
Trainees get a monthly allowance.

examples.ko: 훈련생 모집 공고를 보고 바로 신청했어요.
examples.en: I saw the trainee recruitment notice and applied right away.

examples.ko: 저도 한때는 훈련생이어서 선배들 심부름을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: I was a trainee once too, so I ran a lot of errands for seniors.

explain: 기술이나 직업을 배우는 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 '연수생'은 회사나 기관의 연수 과정에서 많이 쓰고, '훈련생'은 운동이나 기술 훈련에서도 들려요.

phrases.en: I became a cooking trainee this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련 과정에 들어가 배우기 시작했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you have entered a training program and started learning.

phrases.en: The new trainee came for the first time today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 훈련생을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a trainee who has just joined.

phrases.en: They are recruiting trainees next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학원이나 기관에서 훈련생을 뽑는다는 광고나 공지에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in ads and notices from schools or institutions looking for trainees.

explain_en: It is used for someone learning a skill or trade. The similar '연수생' is common for company or institute training programs, while '훈련생' is also heard in sports and technical training.
